[Sweet fucking christ]
; Here there be dragons. Litterally. This series of routines happen when you call Flammie via any method.
; What is the data it's moving around pre and post FlyIn screen? Its used for DMA.
C6/4000:	088B      	PHB 		;Push Data Bank Register.
C6/4002:	C230    	REP #$30	;Enable 16-Bit Accumulator and Index Registers.
C6/4004:	A22000  	LDX #$0020	;Load 0x0020 into Register X. (Source)
C6/4007:	A04010  	LDY #$1040	;Load 0x1040 into Register Y. (Destination)
C6/400A:	A92F00  	LDA #$002F	;Load 0x002F into Accumulator. (Length)
C6/400D:	540000  	MVN $00,$00	;Negative Block Move 0x002F bytes from 00:0020 to 00:1040.
C6/4010:	E220    	SEP #$20	;Disable 16-Bit Accumulator.
C6/4012:	202840  	JSR $4028
C6/4015:	C220    	REP #$20	;Enable 16-Bit Accumulator.
C6/4017:	A24010  	LDX #$1040	;Load 0x1040 into Register X. (Source)
C6/401A:	A02000  	LDY #$0020	;Load 0x0020 into Register Y. (Destination)
C6/401D:	A92F00  	LDA #$002F	;Load 0x002F into Accumulator. (Length)
C6/4020:	540000  	MVN $00,$00	;Negative Block Move 0x002F bytes from 00:1040 to 00:0020.

[WaitFullVerticalBlankCycle]
; So...we have two routines that do the exact same thing, just in reverse?
; Just what?
; This one is used most often. The Redux version is only used by the graphic loader.
C6/459C:	A980		LDA #$80	;Load 0x80 into Accumulator.
C6/459E:	2C1242    	BIT $4212	;Test [PPU Status] to see if we are in V-Blank.
C6/45A1:	D0FB    	BNE $459E	;Branch back up if we aren't in V-Blank.
C6/45A3:	2C1242  	BIT $4212	;Test [PPU Status] to see if we are in V-Blank.
C6/45A6:	F0FB    	BEQ $45A3	;Branch back up if we are in V-Blank.
C6/45A8:	60      	RTS		;Return.

[WaitFullVerticalBlankCycleRedux]
C6/45A9:	AF124200	LDA $004212	;Load [PPU Status] into Accumulator.
C6/45AD:	8980    	BIT #$80	;Test for V-Blank.
C6/45AF:	D0F8    	BNE $45A9	;Branch back up if we are in V-Blank.
C6/45B1:	AF124200	LDA $004212	;Load [PPU Status] into Accumulator.
C6/45B5:	8980    	BIT #$80	;Test for V-Blank.
C6/45B7:	F0F8    	BEQ $45B1	;Branch back up if we aren't in V-Blank.
C6/45B9:	60      	RTS		;Return.

[FadeScreenToBlack]
C6/45BA:	209C45  	JSR $459C	;Jump to WaitFullVerticalBlankCycle.
C6/45BD:	209C45  	JSR $459C	;Jump to WaitFullVerticalBlankCycle.
C6/45C0:	A90F    	LDA #$0F	;Load 0x0F into Accumulator. (Max Brightness)
C6/45C2:	8D0021  	STA $2100	;Store 0x0F into [Screen Display].
C6/45C5:	A90E    	LDA #$0E	;Load 0x0E into Accumulator.
C6/45C7:	48      	PHA		;Push 0x0E into the stack.
C6/45C8:	209C45  	JSR $459C	;Jump to WaitFullVerticalBlankCycle.
C6/45CB:	68      	PLA		;Pull 0x0E off the stack.
C6/45CC:	8D0021  	STA $2100	;Store 0x0E into [Screen Display].
C6/45CF:	3A      	DEC A		;Decrement Accumulator.
C6/45D0:	10F5    	BPL $45C7	;Branch up and continue darkening the screen until Accumulator reaches Zero.
C6/45D2:	60      	RTS		;Return.

[Table_WorldMapLandingLocations]
;     This pile of data controls where you end up when landing on a spot on the World Map.
;     Squaresoft, in their infinite wisdom decided that even though there are 511 maps, you can only land on 256 of them.
;     Then went and made most of those impossible to land on. The first byte is the Map Id to be transported to, the second
;     two bytes are the X/Y coordinates that your characters will be placed at. (The X-Coordinate will be divided by 2).
;     Most of the values in this table are '08 100E' which is the invalid placeholder value, which says "Place characters in the Middle of the New Game Room Map".
;     This happens on purpose a few times by events, but they always transport you to a valid map afterwords.
;     The New Game map also contains an error handler in its OnEnter event incase you manage to get there in some method outside the event system.
;     It will transport you to Potos outside the Inn.
;     
;     Of note is the last entry in this table. Landing on the Mana Fortress will run row 0A. Row FF seems to be a leftover from an older version
;     of the Mana Fortress Exterior map. You get placed outside the map boundries in the lower left corner. I seem to recall a door that places you in
;     the same area, further supporting the idea that the map once had a very different look.
;     
;     It is not a simple hit-test to determine which World Map tile you touched. It is some weird function of the high byte of
;     both your X & Y Coordinates that deterimines which row in this table gets loaded.
067780: 08 100E [00: Map Id: 08 (New Game Room). X-Coordinate: 10, Y-Coordinate: 0E]
067783: 08 100E [01: Map Id: 08 (New Game Room). X-Coordinate: 10, Y-Coordinate: 0E]
067786: 08 100E [02: Map Id: 08 (New Game Room). X-Coordinate: 10, Y-Coordinate: 0E]
067789: 08 100E [03: Map Id: 08 (New Game Room). X-Coordinate: 10, Y-Coordinate: 0E]

[DataTable_FlammieFlightCoordinates]
;     This table controls where on the World Map you end up after using the Flammie Drum.
;     Only the first 256 maps can legally have this ability.
;     First byte is the X-Coordinate, second byte is the Y-Coordinate.
;     
;     The Id of the map that the drum is used on will be used as in index into this table to fetch the flight coordinates.
;     Maps that cannot normally have Flammie called on them will have coordinates somewhere around the Pure Land.
;     
;     The Event System control code 1C can be used to call individual rows, but this is rarely used.

[DataTable_CannonTravelCoordinates]
;     This table is used by Event System control code 1D. It determines where you launch from and land when fired
;     out of a cannon. More then half the entries in this table are invalid and either launch you from, or land you into
;     the ocean. What map you end up on is still controlled by DataTable_WorldMapLandingLocations located at C6/7780.
;     
;     3E and 3F are special in that all though the coordinates are invalid they are used by the game ending and intro respectively
;     with a special flyover effect applied. The events will transport you to valid maps afterwords.

;     For some reason I find travel set 28 to be extremely funny.

[WorldMap_TileConstructionData]
; Okay so, if the byte read is > 0xC0 then AND with 3F and use this byte as a
; counter to draw a tile X number of times where the next byte is the Tile Id.
; If it is <0xC0 then just draw that tile once.
068400: FF B0      ;Draw Tile B0, Repeat 3F Times.
